    Compressed-earth block envelope with designed insulation and heat releasePassive coolingDry and humid heatMeasured in a studyEarth walls provide thermal storage and delay heat transfer; layer placement, insulation and ventilation determine whether stored heat is helpful.

    How it works

    Earth walls provide thermal storage and delay heat transfer; layer placement, insulation and ventilation determine whether stored heat is helpful. Low embodied carbon alone does not establish a cooling benefit.

    Dry or humid heat

    Dry and humid heat. Most direct evidence reviewed is hot-dry: cool nights allow stored heat release; humid warm-night contexts require separate design verification.

    What it has done

    • measured Wall-layer location changed indoor fluctuations; night ventilation improved the experimental building relative to continuous ventilation. No universal °C effect is extracted. Institut 2iE, Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso, 2021 publication; monitoring dates not retained. One unoccupied test building, about 10 m²; three wall arrangements. Limits: Assembly and ventilation effects cannot be attributed to earth alone. Hema et al.: compressed-earth wall experiment (opens in a new tab) ↗

    What makes it work

    Wall thickness, rain protection, insulation, roof and ventilation are designed together for occupancy hours.

    What could stop it

    Insecure tenure/new-build permissions, soil quality, poor detailing, lack of artisans, unsuitable foundations or no nighttime heat sink.

    Rough cost

    Not publicly disclosed in reviewed sources; no universal or inferred price supplied.

    Upkeep

    Owner and trained mason inspect moisture entry, erosion and finish integrity; service life and inspection cadence require local specification.

    Who acts

    National governments, City and local governments, Employers and businesses, Community and civil society groups. Suggested, not commitments.

    Who pays

    Proposed, not committed: household or building owner for private installation; employers for workplace assets; public or philanthropic support where affordability prevents access. Confirm ownership and recurrent payer locally.

    Fairness and risks

    Assess rain/flood erosion, structural approval, transport and binder impacts, indoor space lost to wall thickness and labour safety. Do not market all earth housing as cool or low-cost; confirm women/disabled users can control ventilation safely.

    Where it has been tried

    • Simulation or test Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso, 2021 publication. Compressed-earth/insulation layer arrangements tested. One approximately 10 m² pilot building Hema et al. accepted manuscript (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Evidence

    • Measured in a study Experiment compared wall arrangements and ventilation strategies. Hema et al.: compressed-earth wall experiment (opens in a new tab) ↗
    • Measured in a study Separate Indian CFD work found AAC better insulating than CSEB in the tested scenario; this is modelled, not installed comparative proof. IIT Bombay research account: wall-material CFD (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Moving it elsewhere

    Hot-dry African test-building results cannot be transferred unchanged to hot-humid informal housing; verify seasonal moisture and warm-night behaviour.

    Known, inferred, uncertain

    Known: An actual test building shows arrangement-dependent results.

    Inferred: A locally engineered assembly may reduce overheating while using local materials.

    Uncertain: Two independently identifiable built-location examples and general low-income lifecycle prices were not verified.

    Engineered or plastered bamboo wall assemblyPassive coolingDry and humid heatMeasured in a studyThe complete wall assembly controls heat conduction and thermal delay; bamboo configuration, cavities, plaster and any insulation matter.

    How it works

    The complete wall assembly controls heat conduction and thermal delay; bamboo configuration, cavities, plaster and any insulation matter. Bamboo’s renewability is not proof that a particular wall cools a room.

    Dry or humid heat

    Dry and humid heat. Can be designed for either, but water entry, humidity, thermal mass and fire/structural requirements would be worth assessing locally.

    What it has done

    • measured Array specimens delayed the inner-surface temperature peak more than woven specimens; no room-temperature reduction is inferred. Indonesia; exact test site not stated in inspected paper, 2019 publication. Five wall specimens; specimen 5 compared with woven variants. Limits: Outdoor wall samples, not an occupied building; value converted from 4 h 12 min reported in paper. Risnandar and Wonorahardjo: plastered bamboo wall (opens in a new tab) ↗

    What makes it work

    Assembly is specified for moisture protection, structure, pests, fire safety and local craft capacity.

    What could stop it

    Unsuitable treatment, wet joints, untested structural substitutions, lack of accepted construction details.

    Not publicly disclosed in reviewed sources; no universal or inferred price supplied.

    Upkeep

    Owner/competent builder checks weather protection and joint/pest damage; no generic treatment life or maintenance interval asserted.

    Bio-based phase-change thermal storage in wall panels (emerging)Passive coolingDry and humid heatSimulation or testA phase-change material absorbs heat while melting and releases it while solidifying.

    How it works

    A phase-change material absorbs heat while melting and releases it while solidifying. It shifts heat in time rather than destroying it, so it works only where the daily cycle allows regeneration.

    Dry or humid heat

    Dry and humid heat. Selection depends on phase-change temperature and a sufficiently cool regeneration period; warm humid nights can impede useful discharge.

    What it has done

    • measured The PCM room showed about a 1 °C lower daytime peak and warmer night-time conditions, consistent with thermal storage rather than continuous cooling. Ciawi, Indonesia (highland), 2025 online article; 2026 issue; test date not in abstract. Two rooms, combined floor area 57.6 m²; two consecutive 24-hour cycles. Limits: Short highland test, no severe lowland heatwave or occupant-health evaluation. Universitas Indonesia: coconut-oil PCM bamboo wall experiment (opens in a new tab) ↗

    What makes it work

    Phase-change range matches local temperatures and nighttime conditions regenerate storage.

    What could stop it

    Long warm nights, incomplete solidification, leakage, unsuitable encapsulation or unavailable safe replacement material.

    Rough cost

    Not publicly disclosed in reviewed sources; no universal or inferred price supplied.

    Upkeep

    Panel owner and supplier inspect containment and replace damaged encapsulation; no validated universal service life found.

    Who acts

    Employers and businesses, Community and civil society groups, National governments. Suggested, not commitments.

    Who pays

    Proposed, not committed: household or building owner for private installation; employers for workplace assets; public or philanthropic support where affordability prevents access. Confirm ownership and recurrent payer locally.

    Fairness and risks

    Assess fire performance, leakage, hygiene/pests, replacement cost and evening heat release; it is fairer when poor households do not pay for unproven gains. Disability/gender access and tenure are installation screening questions, not measured study outcomes.

    Where it has been tried

    • Simulation or test Ciawi, Indonesia, 2025 online publication. Experimental PCM-filled versus air-filled bamboo wall panels. Two rooms; total 57.6 m² Universitas Indonesia: coconut-oil PCM bamboo wall experiment (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Evidence

    • Simulation or test Two-room field experiment used coconut-oil PCM inside bamboo panels; the accessible record is an author-institution abstract. Universitas Indonesia: coconut-oil PCM bamboo wall experiment (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Moving it elsewhere

    Do not generalise a highland two-day test to humid lowland bedrooms or claim better sleep.

    Known, inferred, uncertain

    Known: Short-duration thermal smoothing was measured.

    Inferred: Could help where storage cycling matches exposure and occupancy.

    Uncertain: Second deployment location, durability, fire certification, long-duration heatwave benefit and cost are not verified.

    Spectrally engineered daytime radiative-cooling paint (emerging)Passive coolingDry and humid heatReported, not evaluatedAn engineered coating strongly reflects sunlight while emitting thermal infrared toward the sky.

    How it works

    An engineered coating strongly reflects sunlight while emitting thermal infrared toward the sky. Performance depends on atmospheric transmission, sky view and heat exchange; a cool test surface is not automatically a cool occupied room.

    Dry or humid heat

    Substrate, weathering, sky view, optical properties and actual indoor benefit are tested for the intended building.

    What could stop it

    Dust, soiling, moisture, adhesion failure, unsuitable substrate, unverified product claims or high procurement price.

    Passive radiative-cooling film or laminate (emerging)Passive coolingDry and humid heatReported, not evaluatedA solar-reflective, infrared-emitting film reduces solar absorption and radiates heat through the atmospheric window.

    How it works

    A solar-reflective, infrared-emitting film reduces solar absorption and radiates heat through the atmospheric window. Adhesion, substrate and exposed-sky conditions determine performance.

    Dry or humid heat

    Dry and humid heat. Solar rejection can help in either; measured subambient performance in dry clear conditions does not establish humid-season performance.

    What it has done

    • measured An uncovered film specimen averaged 3.9 °C below ambient during the reported Shanghai winter daytime test. University of Shanghai for Science and Technology rooftop, Shanghai, China, 2024-12-24. 5 × 5 cm specimens; number of repeats not stated in inspected passage. Limits: Winter test with average RH 26.02%; not an occupied building; warm-humid transfer not established. Microsphere-polymer radiative-cooling film experiment (opens in a new tab) ↗

    What makes it work

    Actual substrate, waterproofing, adhesion, cleaning and procurement have been verified; sky view is available.

    What could stop it

    Film detachment, soiling, UV/moisture ageing, shading by surrounding structures or inflated model-to-building claims.

    Rough cost

    Not publicly disclosed in reviewed sources; no universal or inferred price supplied.

    Upkeep

    Owner and supplier inspect adhesion and optical condition and clean as product-tested; advertised long lifetime is not accepted as evaluated durability.

    Who acts

    Employers and businesses, City and local governments, Community and civil society groups, National governments. Suggested, not commitments.

    Who pays

    Proposed, not committed: household or building owner for private installation; employers for workplace assets; public or philanthropic support where affordability prevents access. Confirm ownership and recurrent payer locally.

    Fairness and risks

    Assess glare, product toxicity/disposal, worker access and tenant cost recovery. Direct coating operation needs no refrigerant, pump or water; manufacturing burdens still require assessment.

    Where it has been tried

    • Simulation or test Shanghai, China, December 2024; paper 2025. Outdoor film and building-model tests. 5 × 5 cm specimens and model buildings Microsphere-polymer radiative-cooling film experiment (opens in a new tab) ↗
    • Reported, not evaluated Twentynine Palms, California, USA, Exact bench-test date not reported; project anticipated completion 2026. US project account reports subambient surface behaviour, with full demonstration results pending on page. Bench-scale; two-week duration reported US ESTCP radiative-film demonstration project (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Evidence

    • Simulation or test Small specimens and model buildings were measured; annual building savings in the paper are modelled, not measured. Microsphere-polymer radiative-cooling film experiment (opens in a new tab) ↗
    • Reported, not evaluated Official demonstration page reports a bench-scale test and planned building monitoring; targets and advertised life are not verified results. US ESTCP radiative-film demonstration project (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Moving it elsewhere

    Use US case only as a materials/durability learning route; do not import its cost or performance into informal Asian housing.

    Known, inferred, uncertain

    Known: Small-scale tests at two locations are documented.

    Inferred: Film might offer a retrofit form factor if durability and cost are acceptable.

    Uncertain: Independent occupied-house effectiveness, multi-season humid performance, lifecycle cost and complete programme evaluation are not verified.

    Roof pond with intermittent water refresh (low-energy hybrid)Passive coolingDry and humid heatSimulation or testA shallow roof water layer absorbs heat; evaporation and cooler replacement water limit roof heating.

    How it works

    A shallow roof water layer absorbs heat; evaporation and cooler replacement water limit roof heating. The documented system pumps water from an underground tank, so it is low-energy hybrid rather than electricity-free.

    Dry or humid heat

    Dry and humid heat. Evaporation favours dry air; the Kolhapur test also used cooler tank water and night ventilation, so local water temperatures and humidity would be worth checking.

    What it has done

    • measured At 14:00 on the recorded day, roof top temperature was 33.5 °C with the pond versus 48.0 °C without it. Kolhapur, Maharashtra, India, 2019-03-10. One ground-plus-one residence; 57 m² roof. Limits: Single-day comparison; surface result is not indoor reduction. Cost and energy figures are engineering calculations, not independent programme evaluation. Lipare et al.: intermittent-pumping roof pond (opens in a new tab) ↗

    What makes it work

    Engineer verifies wet load, waterproofing, tank, drainage, mosquito control and reliable low-temperature water source.

    What could stop it

    Water scarcity, leaking or structurally unsuitable roof, electricity interruption or no maintenance owner.

    Rough cost

    • Running: undefined INR/day for 57 m² roof. Author engineering calculation: electricity 8 INR/kWh and water 15 INR/kL

    Publication2021; monitoring2019. Cost-base year not explicitly disclosed, so no historical USD conversion inferred. Excludes capital and maintenance. Claimed AC comparisons are not equal-service evaluation. USD conversion withheld because the cost-base year is not verified; do not silently substitute publication year. Lipare et al.: intermittent-pumping roof pond (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Upkeep

    Building owner maintains waterproofing, water tank, pump and sand filter; no validated universal servicing schedule or lifespan was supplied.

    Who acts

    Community and civil society groups, Employers and businesses, City and local governments, Water authorities. Suggested, not commitments.

    Who pays

    Proposed, not committed: household or building owner for private installation; employers for workplace assets; public or philanthropic support where affordability prevents access. Confirm ownership and recurrent payer locally.

    Fairness and risks

    Reported engineering calculation uses 342 L evaporation and 0.735 kWh pumping per day; substantial water burden makes this unsuitable as a default poorest-household option. Check child safety, roof access, gendered water labour and rents. No refrigerant, but pump electricity and water supply carry impacts.

    Where it has been tried

    • Simulation or test Kolhapur, Maharashtra, India, 2019 monitoring; 2021 publication. Intermittently refreshed roof pond with underground storage. One residence; 57 m² roof Lipare et al.: intermittent-pumping roof pond (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Evidence

    • Simulation or test Small field study measured roof and room temperatures; paper also calculated water, pumping and costs. Lipare et al.: intermittent-pumping roof pond (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Moving it elsewhere

    Transfer only after structural/water-budget review; do not equate surface cooling with heat-health protection or claim equivalence to AC.

    Known, inferred, uncertain

    Known: A real building was tested and resource use estimated.

    Inferred: Could be feasible for selected structures with suitable water infrastructure.

    Uncertain: Second tried location for this exact configuration, long-duration performance, upkeep price and cost-base year were not verified.

    Street trees and retained mature canopyPassive coolingDry and humid heatMeasured in a studyCanopy intercepts solar radiation before it reaches people and surfaces; transpiration can additionally shift heat into water vapour.

    How it works

    Canopy intercepts solar radiation before it reaches people and surfaces; transpiration can additionally shift heat into water vapour.

    Dry or humid heat

    Dry and humid heat. Shade is useful in both; evaporative benefit needs water and can add humidity. Canopy density, species and wind matter.

    What it has done

    • measured Maximum air-temperature reductions under dense canopy were 2.3–3°C, versus 1.2–1.4°C under sparse canopy. Pathum Thani university parking-lot trial, Thailand, December2019/April2020; published2022. Dense and sparse tree clusters plus three artificial canopy materials; no independent-site replication reported. Limits: A small field trial; maxima are not daily averages and do not isolate transpiration from shade. Jareemit and Srivanit, market shade and tree canopy field trial (opens in a new tab) ↗

    What makes it work

    Keep existing mature trees where safe; choose canopy and placement for occupied routes and resting areas.

    What could stop it

    Check rooting space, utilities, permissions, drought and establishment watering.

    Rough cost

    No comparable item-level priced bill with price year and separated capex/opex/upkeep was verified. No price or FX inferred.

    Upkeep

    Assign arboricultural inspection, establishment watering and replacement to an accountable owner; local intervals need specification.

    Who acts

    City and local governments, Community and civil society groups, Employers and businesses, Schools and education authorities, Water authorities. Suggested, not commitments.

    Who pays

    Proposed route: responsible local authority, site owner or employer funds capital and recurring maintenance; grants can support equitable access. No named financing commitment inferred.

    Fairness and risks

    Screen whether shade reaches women traders and wheelchair users; protect trading/tenure rights; test wind obstruction and water demand rather than assuming all greenery cools equally.

    Where it has been tried

    • Measured in a study Pathum Thani, Thailand, 2019–2020 fieldwork. Existing tree clusters compared with unshaded conditions and experimental market canopies. Two canopy-density settings Jareemit and Srivanit, market shade and tree canopy field trial (opens in a new tab) ↗
    • Measured in a study Roorkee canal-front sites, India, Summer2022; published2025. Field study of existing green-blue configurations, including tree shade. Sample count not in reviewed abstract Manavvi and Milosevic, Chasing cool, Roorkee (opens in a new tab) ↗

    • Measured in a study See the mechanism, effect or implementation example for the specific finding; this evidence label describes kind, not effectiveness. Manavvi and Milosevic, Chasing cool, Roorkee (opens in a new tab) ↗
    • Measured in a study See the mechanism, effect or implementation example for the specific finding; this evidence label describes kind, not effectiveness. Lin et al., Street spatial structure, Taipei (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Retain or restore urban lakes and ponds with climate screeningPassive coolingDry and humid heatMeasured in a studyWater exchanges sensible and latent heat with its surroundings; its thermal storage can moderate daytime conditions but release heat at night.

    How it works

    Water exchanges sensible and latent heat with its surroundings; its thermal storage can moderate daytime conditions but release heat at night.

    Dry or humid heat

    Dry and humid heat. Potential daytime cooling in both; hot-dry use needs a defensible water budget, while humid conditions can amplify nighttime heat and moisture.

    What it has done

    • measured Against rural sites, daytime lake cool-island intensity was 0.1–0.6°C but warm-season nighttime heat-island intensity was 1.2–1.3°C. Nanjing and Guangzhou, China, Published2023; exact monitoring dates not in reviewed abstract. One year continuous monitoring of lake, residential and rural sites in two cities; site count not in abstract. Limits: Not a before-after restoration trial; a different residential baseline gives a different interpretation. No reduction in mortality established. Yao et al., urban lakes in Nanjing and Guangzhou (opens in a new tab) ↗

    What makes it work

    Evaluate daytime and nighttime air, humidity and access; retain safe ecological function and water quality.

    What could stop it

    Check water scarcity, polluted inflows, mosquito control, banks and drowning hazards.

    Rough cost

    No comparable item-level priced bill with price year and separated capex/opex/upkeep was verified. No price or FX inferred.

    Upkeep

    Water authority/site manager needs water-quality, vegetation and safety maintenance; pumping energy would be worth separately disclosing if used.

    Who acts

    City and local governments, Water authorities, Community and civil society groups. Suggested, not commitments.

    Who pays

    Proposed route: responsible local authority, site owner or employer funds capital and recurring maintenance; grants can support equitable access. No named financing commitment inferred.

    Fairness and risks

    Do not frame added humidity as harmless; check flood safety, accessible edges, land rights and water allocation before creating new water features.

    • Measured in a study Guangzhou, China, One-year study; published2023. Existing urban lake thermal behaviour measured. Lake/residential/rural site network; count not in abstract Yao et al., urban lakes in Nanjing and Guangzhou (opens in a new tab) ↗

    An overhead or lateral opaque cover blocks direct solar radiation; material, height and sun angle determine how much of the occupied space remains shaded.

    • measured Across multiple shade types, average MRT decreased10°C while air temperature decreased0.8°C. Limits: Aggregate across shade types; cannot attribute the full10°C to a particular sail/material. Xu et al., street shade in Singapore (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Reflective cool pavements with pedestrian radiation screeningPassive coolingDry and humid heatMeasured in a studyHigher solar reflectance reduces absorbed energy and surface heat storage, but sends additional shortwave radiation towards surrounding people and buildings.

    How it works

    Higher solar reflectance reduces absorbed energy and surface heat storage, but sends additional shortwave radiation towards surrounding people and buildings.

    What it has done

    • measured Mean air cooling immediately after sunset was0.3°C across studied neighbourhoods; daytime air effects were much smaller than surface effects. Phoenix, Arizona, USA, 2020 pilot; publication2023. Three treated/control neighbourhood comparisons; two vehicle traverses in four daily windows. Schneider et al., reflective pavement field study, Phoenix (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Assess air, surface and MRT separately; combine exposed pedestrian routes with shade and inspect reflectance decay.

    What could stop it

    Check glare, road safety, local climate, pavement condition and replacement/renewal costs.

    No comparable item-level priced bill with price year and separated capex/opex/upkeep was verified. No price or FX inferred.

    Related practical actions: Markets and neighbourhoods · Schools and childcare · Before summer: for municipalities

    Climate-responsive street orientation and canyon geometryPassive coolingDry and humid heatMeasured in a studyBuilding height, street width and orientation alter solar access, longwave heat loss and airflow; improving one can compromise another.

    How it works

    Building height, street width and orientation alter solar access, longwave heat loss and airflow; improving one can compromise another.

    Dry or humid heat

    Dry and humid heat. Both require local solar/wind design. Deep canyons can shade daytime exposure but may constrain wind or nighttime heat loss.

    What it has done

    • measured Measurements found different shade and microclimate conditions across six street canyons; not a before/after redesign experiment. Daan District, Taipei, Hot/cool season2019; publication2024. Six canyons with aspect ratio1; each location observed in hot and cool seasons. Limits: Nonrandomised existing-street comparisons; contextual urban factors remain. Lin et al., Street spatial structure, Taipei (opens in a new tab) ↗

    What makes it work

    Evaluate local shade, ventilation, nighttime conditions and air quality before design approval.

    What could stop it

    Retrofitting street geometry may require land, redevelopment and rights protections; do not assume a model optimum is implementable.

    Rough cost

    No comparable item-level priced bill with price year and separated capex/opex/upkeep was verified. No price or FX inferred.

    Upkeep

    Built geometry is long-lived; planning/design owners would ideally preserve ventilation routes and maintain shaded walking access; life not quantified.

    Who acts

    City and local governments, National governments, Community and civil society groups, Employers and businesses. Suggested, not commitments.

    Who pays

    Proposed route: responsible local authority, site owner or employer funds capital and recurring maintenance; grants can support equitable access. No named financing commitment inferred.

    Fairness and risks

    Screen demolition/displacement, density/access trade-offs and pollutant trapping; local recommendations need resident and trader input.

    Where it has been tried

    • Measured in a study Daan EW4 street site, Taipei, 2019 fieldwork; published2024. Existing built street form measured; not a newly installed intervention. One east–west site among six Lin et al., Street spatial structure, Taipei (opens in a new tab) ↗
    • Measured in a study Daan NS4 street site, Taipei, 2019 fieldwork; published2024. Different existing street orientation observed; not a second city. One north–south site among six Lin et al., Street spatial structure, Taipei (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Evidence

    • Measured in a study See the mechanism, effect or implementation example for the specific finding; this evidence label describes kind, not effectiveness. Lin et al., Street spatial structure, Taipei (opens in a new tab) ↗
    • Measured in a study Study analyses a modelled scenario; measured label identifies study/analysis, not a field-proven intervention. Acero et al., high-rise urban geometry, Singapore (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Moving it elsewhere

    Transfer mechanism rather than a numerical cooling promise. Check solar geometry, wind, humidity, water budget, access rights and maintenance capacity locally. High-income examples supply design or measurement lessons, not transferable prices.

    Known, inferred, uncertain

    Known: Existing street measurements and Singapore scenario analysis show context-sensitive geometry effects.

    Inferred: Solar/wind review belongs upstream in planning and redevelopment decisions.

    Uncertain: Causal welfare effect of changing geometry and transferable optimal orientation are not established.

    Schoolyard greening, depaving and shade as a coordinated retrofitPassive coolingDry and humid heatMeasured in a studyReplace selected exposed hard surfaces with shaded planted/permeable spaces and usable outdoor refuge; thermal contributions of the combined package cannot fairly be assigned to one component.

    How it works

    Replace selected exposed hard surfaces with shaded planted/permeable spaces and usable outdoor refuge; thermal contributions of the combined package cannot fairly be assigned to one component.

    Dry or humid heat

    Dry and humid heat. Both require locally suitable planting, shade and a water/maintenance plan; a European package is not an Asian thermal guarantee.

    What it has done

    • measured Community users described shade as comfortable; this is qualitative experience rather than a measured degree reduction. Barcelona, Spain, June–July2022; publication2025. 22 observations at11 schoolyards; interviews with76 users and18 caretakers. Limits: Package also included water features, including misters; passive greening/shade effect not isolated. Study by public-health agency, not automatically independent programme evaluation. Sanz-Mas et al., Community use and perceptions of schoolyard climate shelters (opens in a new tab) ↗

    What makes it work

    Co-design with children/staff, retain accessible play and toilets, define responsibility for watering and public opening.

    What could stop it

    Check school security, cleaning, surveillance budgets, water use and time needed for trees to grow.

    Rough cost

    No comparable item-level priced bill with price year and separated capex/opex/upkeep was verified. No price or FX inferred.

    Upkeep

    School/city teams need planted-space, cleaning and access-management arrangements; published programme maintenance guide exists.

    Who acts

    Schools and education authorities, City and local governments, Community and civil society groups, Water authorities, Health authorities. Suggested, not commitments.

    Who pays

    Proposed route: responsible local authority, site owner or employer funds capital and recurring maintenance; grants can support equitable access. No named financing commitment inferred.

    Fairness and risks

    Study observed more boys among users. Screen age/gender differences and disability access; opening gates alone does not ensure equitable use.

    Where it has been tried

    • Reported, not evaluated Paris OASIS schoolyards, France, Programme since2017; official updateJanuary2025. Co-designed transformed yards; counts are programme reports, not evaluated thermal outcomes. 203 schoolyards and5 nursery courtyards reported by city City of Paris, Les cours oasis (opens in a new tab) ↗
    • Measured in a study Barcelona climate-shelter schoolyards, Spain, Transformed2020; use studied2022. Combined green/blue/grey retrofit; passive components only are relevant to this library. 11 primary schoolyards Sanz-Mas et al., Community use and perceptions of schoolyard climate shelters (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Evidence

    • Reported, not evaluated See the mechanism, effect or implementation example for the specific finding; this evidence label describes kind, not effectiveness. City of Paris, Les cours oasis (opens in a new tab) ↗
    • Measured in a study See the mechanism, effect or implementation example for the specific finding; this evidence label describes kind, not effectiveness. Sanz-Mas et al., Community use and perceptions of schoolyard climate shelters (opens in a new tab) ↗
    • Official guidance or data See the mechanism, effect or implementation example for the specific finding; this evidence label describes kind, not effectiveness. EEA Climate-ADAPT, OASIS case study (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Moving it elsewhere

    Transfer mechanism rather than a numerical cooling promise. Check solar geometry, wind, humidity, water budget, access rights and maintenance capacity locally. High-income examples supply design or measurement lessons, not transferable prices.

    Known, inferred, uncertain

    Known: Both cities implemented schoolyard packages; Barcelona provides measured qualitative use evidence.

    Inferred: Distributed school grounds could extend neighbourhood access where governance permits.

    Uncertain: Transferable LMIC cost, isolated thermal effect and long-term learning/health outcomes remain uncertain.

    On the map, it can help break: The lost-schooling loop

    Shade-tree agroforestry for cropsPassive coolingDry and humid heatMeasured in a studyTree canopies intercept sunlight and modify the crop microclimate.

    How it works

    Tree canopies intercept sunlight and modify the crop microclimate. Cooling and moisture effects depend on canopy structure and crop placement.

    Dry or humid heat

    Dry and humid heat. Both, conditionally. Studies document dry-season daytime moderation and humid coffee settings; species, canopy gaps, water competition and disease conditions need local assessment. Climate transfer is an analytical inference, not a universal suitability finding.

    What it has done

    • measured Air temperature ranged from 42.56°C in the treeless control to 38.44°C under Karanj in the Teak–Karanj treatment in the reported spatial comparison. Plandu/Churu experimental farm, Ranchi, India, 2021 measurements; published 2026. Five treatments, four replications; established 2016; sampling March–June at 15-day intervals. Limits: Not human heat exposure or crop-yield effect; different positions/treatments; do not present a universal 4.12°C cooling guarantee. Khanna et al., multitier agroforestry, Indian Journal of Agroforestry 2026 (opens in a new tab) ↗

    What makes it work

    Crop light requirements and canopy arrangement are matched; benefit is checked at actual worker/crop positions.

    What could stop it

    Screen tenure, delayed canopy establishment, competition for light/water and lack of tree-care capacity.

    Rough cost

    Not publicly disclosed as separable cooling costs in reviewed sources; no global price inferred.

    Upkeep

    Establish responsibility for tree survival, pruning and replacement; no universal service life or schedule verified.

    Who acts

    Farmers’ organisations and agriculture agencies, Community and civil society groups, National governments. Suggested, not commitments.

    Who pays

    Proposed responsibility: landowner or employer, with grant/public support where needed. No financing commitment is implied.

    Fairness and risks

    Screen who can access the cooling, who controls land and finance, and who carries unpaid maintenance. Do not infer gender or disability outcomes from these thermal studies.

    Where it has been tried

    • Measured in a study Plandu/Churu, Ranchi, India, Established 2016; measurements 2021. Teak/Karanj with pigeon pea or chickpea. Five treatments, four replications Khanna et al., multitier agroforestry, Indian Journal of Agroforestry 2026 (opens in a new tab) ↗
    • Measured in a study Pujon, Malang, East Java, Indonesia, Published 2024; observation dates not reported in abstract. Coffee under pine, lamtoro and durian shade. Purposive farmer sample; number not reported in abstract Triwanto et al., coffee agroforestry microclimate, Pujon 2024 (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Evidence

    • Measured in a study A replicated field experiment measured canopy-linked microclimate; temperature varied with tree species and position. Khanna et al., multitier agroforestry, Indian Journal of Agroforestry 2026 (opens in a new tab) ↗
    • Measured in a study Direct observation of coffee agroforestry in Pujon described shaded microclimates; no unshaded causal cooling estimate is extracted. Triwanto et al., coffee agroforestry microclimate, Pujon 2024 (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Moving it elsewhere

    In dry sites assess tree-water competition and establishment; humid sites require canopy/airflow and crop-disease checks. Species, crop, canopy maturity and actual worker positions change the outcome.

    Known, inferred, uncertain

    Known: Field microclimates differ under tree arrangements.

    Inferred: Appropriate shade may reduce exposure at work locations.

    Uncertain: Human health/income effects and affordable establishment/maintenance costs were not verified.

    On the map, it can help break: The dry-soil loop · The groundwater loop

    Related practical actions: Outdoor and hot workplaces · Before summer: for municipalities

    Silvopasture: trees integrated with grazing livestockPassive coolingDry and humid heatMeasured in a studyTrees shade animals from solar radiation and provide a different grazing microclimate from open pasture.

    How it works

    Trees shade animals from solar radiation and provide a different grazing microclimate from open pasture.

    Dry or humid heat

    Dry and humid heat. Both, conditionally. Tropical and subtropical Brazilian field studies support shade use; transfer to hot-dry Asia requires suitable tree survival and water, while humid sites need airflow. This transfer assessment is inference.

    What it has done

    • measured Shaded cattle had lower body temperatures, respiratory rates and panting scores than full-sun cattle; no pooled numerical reduction is extracted. Brazilian Cerrado, Two-year observation period; published 2026; calendar observation dates not extracted. 48 lactating cows: 24 Gyr and 24 Girolando. Limits: Animal outcomes, not evidence of worker protection; breed and local management matter. McManus et al., Shade matters, 2026 (opens in a new tab) ↗
    • measured Silvopasture cows showed lower respiratory rates in summer/fall and lower rectal temperature in spring/fall. Brazilian subtropical site, Warm season spanning spring, summer and fall; published 2021; exact site/date not available in abstract. 12 lactating Jersey cows. Limits: Season-specific result; abstract only reviewed. Skonieski et al., Jersey cows in silvopasture, 2021 (opens in a new tab) ↗

    What makes it work

    Animals can actually access sufficient shade during hot periods; design and grazing management match the herd.

    What could stop it

    Screen land tenure, tree establishment, fodder/light trade-offs and tree-care responsibilities.

    Rough cost

    Not publicly disclosed as separable cooling costs in reviewed sources; no global price inferred.

    Upkeep

    Assign tree and grazing management to the land/herd operator; no universal inspection interval verified.

    Who acts

    Farmers’ organisations and agriculture agencies, Community and civil society groups, National governments. Suggested, not commitments.

    Who pays

    Proposed responsibility: landowner or employer, with grant/public support where needed. No financing commitment is implied.

    Fairness and risks

    Screen who can access the cooling, who controls land and finance, and who carries unpaid maintenance. Do not infer gender or disability outcomes from these thermal studies. Screen whether smallholders can finance establishment and whether communal grazing users retain access; tree planting is not an immediate replacement for existing shade.

    Where it has been tried

    • Measured in a study Brazilian Cerrado, Brazil, Published 2026; monitored for two years. Eucalyptus urograndis shade versus full sun. 48 lactating cattle McManus et al., Shade matters, 2026 (opens in a new tab) ↗
    • Measured in a study Subtropical Brazil, Published 2021. Eucalyptus silvopasture versus treeless conventional pasture; precise study municipality not verified in abstract. 12 lactating Jersey cows Skonieski et al., Jersey cows in silvopasture, 2021 (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Evidence

    • Measured in a study Monitored animals under tree shade and full sun. McManus et al., Shade matters, 2026 (opens in a new tab) ↗
    • Measured in a study Compared tree-integrated and conventional grazing systems. Skonieski et al., Jersey cows in silvopasture, 2021 (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Moving it elsewhere

    Adapt tree species, herd breed, stocking and shade access; dry-site establishment and humid-site ventilation differ. Animal studies cannot establish human health effects.

    Known, inferred, uncertain

    Known: Cattle physiological responses improved under studied tree-integrated systems.

    Inferred: The mechanism may transfer with adapted species and adequate shade access.

    Uncertain: No generic yield gain, Asian cost, worker-health benefit or guaranteed animal safety threshold is established.

    Related practical actions: Outdoor and hot workplaces · Before summer: for municipalities

    Artificial shade shelters for livestockPassive coolingDry and humid heatSimulation or testAn overhead shading material intercepts solar radiation before it reaches animals.

    How it works

    An overhead shading material intercepts solar radiation before it reaches animals. Material and ventilation change the radiant environment beneath it.

    Dry or humid heat

    Dry and humid heat. Both, conditionally. Tropical Brazilian and hot-humid Indian calf studies support shading; retain air movement and avoid treating a hot enclosed shed as equivalent to open shade.

    What it has done

    • measured Artificial shade had mean radiant temperature below 30°C during daylight and radiant heat load below 470 W/m²; both were lower than natural shade in the study. Tropical Brazilian pasture; exact site not specified in reviewed abstract, Published February 2026; field dates not stated in abstract. Eight multiparous Holstein cows over 20 nonconsecutive days. Limits: Absolute ranges, not a cooling delta; small trial and specific double-net structure. Barcelos et al., natural and artificial shade, 2026 (opens in a new tab) ↗
    • measured Agro-net treatment had lower microclimate and physiological heat indicators than the other roof treatments during rainy-season observations. Indian ICAR study; precise experiment location not verified in abstract, Published 2016; rainy-season field dates not stated. 18 calves in three groups. Limits: Do not recommend asbestos; existing comparator is not an acceptable specification. Kamal et al., shade materials for calves, 2016 (opens in a new tab) ↗

    What makes it work

    Material, geometry and access are assessed for the animals and local conditions; the tested structure is not a universal design.

    What could stop it

    Screen wind anchorage, structural safety, fabric deterioration and crowding beneath limited shade.

    Rough cost

    Not publicly disclosed as separable cooling costs in reviewed sources; no global price inferred.

    Upkeep

    Assign anchorage and fabric/roof inspection and replacement; no verified universal lifespan or schedule.

    Who acts

    Farmers’ organisations and agriculture agencies, Employers and businesses, Community and civil society groups. Suggested, not commitments.

    Who pays

    Proposed responsibility: landowner or employer, with grant/public support where needed. No financing commitment is implied.

    Fairness and risks

    Screen who can access the cooling, who controls land and finance, and who carries unpaid maintenance. Do not infer gender or disability outcomes from these thermal studies.

    Where it has been tried

    • Simulation or test Brazil, tropical pasture, Published 2026. Artificial double-net shade compared with natural shade. Eight cows, two paddocks Barcelos et al., natural and artificial shade, 2026 (opens in a new tab) ↗
    • Simulation or test India, Published 2016. Agro-net shade compared with other shelter roofs in rainy season. 18 crossbred calves Kamal et al., shade materials for calves, 2016 (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Evidence

    • Simulation or test Measured an aluminized outer net and black polypropylene inner net structure against natural shade. Barcelos et al., natural and artificial shade, 2026 (opens in a new tab) ↗
    • Simulation or test Small calf trial compared three shade-roof materials. Kamal et al., shade materials for calves, 2016 (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Moving it elsewhere

    Adapt fabric optical properties, height, anchorage, occupied shade area and ventilation; test rather than transferring a Brazilian double-net or Indian calf result directly.

    Known, inferred, uncertain

    Known: Specific shade structures altered radiant and animal heat responses.

    Inferred: An appropriately designed shelter can transfer the shading mechanism without operating electricity.

    Uncertain: Longevity, replacement frequency, affordability and Asia-wide performance were not verified.

    Related practical actions: Outdoor and hot workplaces · Before summer: for municipalities

    Mobile shaded rest shelters for agricultural workersPassive coolingDry and humid heatMeasured in a studyA movable canopy intercepts direct sunlight at a rest location near the work area.

    How it works

    A movable canopy intercepts direct sunlight at a rest location near the work area. It is the physical shade component of a broader work-rest-water arrangement.

    Dry or humid heat

    Dry and humid heat. Both, conditionally. Shade reduces direct solar exposure but does not eliminate high air temperature/humidity or metabolic heat; it works only if users can take breaks. Climate transfer is analytical inference.

    What it has done

    • measured Across-harvest estimated glomerular filtration decline was −3.4 mL/min/1.73m² in the intervention group and −5.3 in the comparison group. El Salvador sugarcane fields, Harvest November 2014–April 2015; paper 2018. 40 intervention and 40 comparison workers completed baseline/end harvest. Limits: Whole water–rest–shade plus efficiency bundle; nonrandomized groups. Cannot attribute kidney effect to canopy or infer prevention of chronic kidney disease. Wegman et al., WRS intervention, El Salvador, 2018 (opens in a new tab) ↗

    What makes it work

    Shade stays near moving work and workers can use scheduled breaks; the canopy is not a substitute for water, rest and work organisation.

    What could stop it

    Security concerns delayed a planned intervention in the El Salvador comparison group. Screen piece-rate income and supervisors’ ability to maintain accessible rest.

    Rough cost

    Not publicly disclosed as separable cooling costs in reviewed sources; no global price inferred.

    Upkeep

    Employer or operator would ideally move, inspect and keep the shelter usable alongside work-rest arrangements; inspection frequency not established by extracted evidence.

    Who acts

    Employers and businesses, Worker organisations and unions, Farmers’ organisations and agriculture agencies, Health authorities, Community and civil society groups. Suggested, not commitments.

    Who pays

    Verified example: El Ángel mill funded the interventions; research funding came from Dutch National Postcode Lottery via Solidaridad. Proposed transfer: employer finances access and operating arrangements, with worker participation.

    Fairness and risks

    Screen who can access the cooling, who controls land and finance, and who carries unpaid maintenance. Do not infer gender or disability outcomes from these thermal studies. Examine paid-rest arrangements and equitable access for women, migrants and workers with disabilities; the bundle study does not establish outcomes for every subgroup.

    Where it has been tried

    • Measured in a study El Ángel mill work areas, El Salvador, 2014–2015 harvest; published 2018. Mobile shade moved with cutters; rest and water provided alongside work changes. 80 end-harvest participants across intervention/comparison groups Wegman et al., WRS intervention, El Salvador, 2018 (opens in a new tab) ↗
    • Measured in a study Ingenio San Antonio, Chichigalpa, Nicaragua, Published 2025; four harvests described. Progressively enhanced rest–shade–hydration–hygiene intervention. Cohort size not extracted from accessible abstract Hansson et al., RSHH cohort, Nicaragua, 2025 (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Evidence

    • Measured in a study Field intervention supplied mobile shade tents, scheduled rest and water with efficiency changes; measured kidney biomarkers. Wegman et al., WRS intervention, El Salvador, 2018 (opens in a new tab) ↗
    • Measured in a study Nicaraguan cohort assessed a progressively enhanced rest–shade–hydration–hygiene programme; programme bundle, not a canopy-only effect. Hansson et al., RSHH cohort, Nicaragua, 2025 (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Moving it elsewhere

    Adapt mobility to work patterns, break access to employment/payment arrangements, and water/toilet provision to the local setting. High humidity or hot air can leave substantial residual exposure beneath shade.

    Known, inferred, uncertain

    Known: Mobile tents were implemented within studied work-rest-water packages.

    Inferred: Accessible shade tends to last when financed together with operating and income arrangements.

    Uncertain: The separate causal contribution or price of shade, transfer to smallholder/informal work and chronic-disease prevention remain unestablished.

    Related practical actions: Outdoor and hot workplaces · Before summer: for municipalities

    Shade-net structures for crop microclimate protectionPassive coolingDry and humid heatMeasured in a studyA porous shading cover reduces incoming solar radiation while allowing air exchange.

    How it works

    A porous shading cover reduces incoming solar radiation while allowing air exchange. It alters crop light, temperature and humidity rather than mechanically cooling the air.

    Dry or humid heat

    Dry and humid heat. Both, conditionally. A hot-arid Jodhpur trial demonstrated different temperatures/humidity among protected structures. In humid settings, airflow, crop disease and excessive shading require local testing; crop benefits cannot be assumed.

    What it has done

    • measured Shade-net house air temperature was 0.7°C lower and relative humidity four percent higher than insect-proof net house in the cited hot-arid comparison. Jodhpur, Rajasthan, India, Published 2021; crop field dates not stated in reviewed abstract. Three protected structure types; replication not extracted. Limits: Not a universal shade-net reduction; do not equate crop microclimate with worker safety. Khapte et al., protected cultivation in Jodhpur, 2021 (opens in a new tab) ↗

    What makes it work

    Shading density, crop light needs and ventilation are matched; trial shows structure choice changes humidity as well as temperature.

    What could stop it

    Screen wind safety, replacement fabric, crop shading penalties, poor ventilation and finance/tenure constraints.

    Rough cost

    Not publicly disclosed as separable cooling costs in reviewed sources; no global price inferred.

    Upkeep

    Grower/operator would ideally inspect nets, anchorage and crop ventilation and budget replacement; service life not verified.

    Who acts

    Farmers’ organisations and agriculture agencies, Employers and businesses, Community and civil society groups. Suggested, not commitments.

    Who pays

    Proposed responsibility: landowner or employer, with grant/public support where needed. No financing commitment is implied.

    Fairness and risks

    Screen who can access the cooling, who controls land and finance, and who carries unpaid maintenance. Do not infer gender or disability outcomes from these thermal studies.

    Where it has been tried

    • Measured in a study Jodhpur, Rajasthan, India, Published 2021. Cucumber microclimate comparison. Three protected cultivation structure types Khapte et al., protected cultivation in Jodhpur, 2021 (opens in a new tab) ↗
    • Measured in a study Ludhiana, Punjab, India, Winter 2021–22 and spring 2022; published 2025. Shade net and polyethylene protective-cover study; not a pure canopy-only cooling estimate. Two French bean varieties; control and three cover-timing treatments Rani et al., French bean shade net and polyethylene, Punjab, 2025 (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Evidence

    • Measured in a study Compared naturally ventilated polyhouse, insect-proof net house and shade-net house. Khapte et al., protected cultivation in Jodhpur, 2021 (opens in a new tab) ↗
    • Measured in a study Ludhiana trial compared crop-cover timing with uncovered French bean; polyethylene and shade-net components require separation before attributing cooling. Rani et al., French bean shade net and polyethylene, Punjab, 2025 (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Moving it elsewhere

    Shade density and ventilation would ideally match crop, season and humidity. Do not transfer a cucumber crop microclimate result to human safety or to every protected structure.

    Known, inferred, uncertain

    Known: Protected structure configuration changes crop microclimate.

    Inferred: Shade-net design can be a low-operating-energy heat-adaptation component.

    Uncertain: A universal optimum shading fraction, worker-health benefit and lowest-cost design were not established.

    On the map, it can help break: The groundwater loop · The farm-debt loop

    Related practical actions: Outdoor and hot workplaces · Before summer: for municipalities

    Organic residue mulch for cooler crop root zonesPassive coolingDry and humid heatMeasured in a studyA cover of organic residues shades and buffers the soil surface, altering soil temperature and moisture exchange.

    How it works

    A cover of organic residues shades and buffers the soil surface, altering soil temperature and moisture exchange. This is root-zone heat management, not proof of cooler breathing-height air.

    Dry or humid heat

    Dry and humid heat. Both, conditionally. Indian and coastal Bangladeshi studies support context-dependent soil moderation; dryland Iraq also tested straw. Wetness, season and mulch material matter: some plastics intentionally warm soils.

    What it has done

    • measured Organic-mulch treatments had soil temperatures 25.0–27.3°C, versus 27.9°C without mulch; synthetic treatments were warmer at 28.3–32.8°C. Ultakhali village, Amtali, Barguna, Bangladesh, Rabi 2022–23 and 2023–24; publication 2025. Eight treatments, four replications. Limits: Range spans organic materials; not air temperature, worker exposure or a guaranteed rice-straw-only delta. Haque et al., organic and synthetic mulch, coastal Bangladesh, 2025 (opens in a new tab) ↗
    • measured At 15/30/45 days after planting, mulched/FYM trial soil means were 26.2/30.3/31.7°C versus 27.0/32.3/32.5°C under farmer practice. Lumami village, Zunheboto, Nagaland, India, Field dates not reported in abstract; 2021 issue, online 2022. Three one-hectare jhum fields. Limits: Mulch and farmyard manure applied together; temperatures do not isolate mulch alone. Sentimenla, paddy-straw mulch and FYM, Nagaland (opens in a new tab) ↗

    What makes it work

    Select mulch for the season and crop; confirm soil cooling rather than assuming all ground covers cool.

    What could stop it

    Screen residue availability, alternative fodder/fuel use, transport/labour, pest conditions, drainage and fire exposure.

    Rough cost

    Not publicly disclosed as separable cooling costs in reviewed sources; no global price inferred.

    Upkeep

    Grower would ideally maintain intended cover and assess decomposition and seasonal replacement; no universal replenishment frequency verified.

    Who acts

    Farmers’ organisations and agriculture agencies, Community and civil society groups. Suggested, not commitments.

    Who pays

    Proposed responsibility: landowner or employer, with grant/public support where needed. No financing commitment is implied.

    Fairness and risks

    Screen who can access the cooling, who controls land and finance, and who carries unpaid maintenance. Do not infer gender or disability outcomes from these thermal studies. Do not treat residues as free where they have other livelihood uses. Assign labour and access to residues fairly. Plastic cover is not interchangeable with organic cooling mulch.

    Where it has been tried

    • Measured in a study Ultakhali, Amtali, Barguna, Bangladesh, 2022–23 and 2023–24. Sweet gourd in coastal saline soils. Eight mulch/control treatments, four replicates Haque et al., organic and synthetic mulch, coastal Bangladesh, 2025 (opens in a new tab) ↗
    • Measured in a study Lumami, Zunheboto, Nagaland, India, Published 2021 issue/2022 online; field dates not stated. Paddy-straw and FYM trial with colocasia. Three one-hectare fields Sentimenla, paddy-straw mulch and FYM, Nagaland (opens in a new tab) ↗
    • Measured in a study University of Wasit experimental field, Iraq, July–November 2019. Straw/palm-frond/black-nylon/no-mulch comparison with irrigation methods. 24 experimental units, three replications Al-Lame and Al-Saadoon, soil mulch and irrigation, Iraq (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Evidence

    • Measured in a study Replicated two-season trial distinguished cooler organic from warmer synthetic mulch treatments. Haque et al., organic and synthetic mulch, coastal Bangladesh, 2025 (opens in a new tab) ↗
    • Measured in a study Farm trials measured soil temperature under straw plus farmyard manure. Sentimenla, paddy-straw mulch and FYM, Nagaland (opens in a new tab) ↗
    • Measured in a study Replicated 2019 field trial found straw cooler than control/black nylon, demonstrating a dryland comparison. Al-Lame and Al-Saadoon, soil mulch and irrigation, Iraq (opens in a new tab) ↗
    • Measured in a study Winter tomato trial found plastic mulch warming at night; higher yield alone is not evidence of heat cooling. Sultana et al., mulch and soil temperature, Assam, 2026 (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Moving it elsewhere

    Transfer by soil, crop, rainfall, salinity, material and season. Separate cooling from desired winter warming; soil-temperature changes cannot be relabelled air or body-temperature changes.

    Known, inferred, uncertain

    Known: Specific organic mulches moderated soil heat in cited experiments; plastics may warm soil.

    Inferred: Locally available residues may be a useful low-energy crop protection component.

    Uncertain: Net costs, labour distribution, long-term effects and human heat-health benefits were not verified.

    On the map, it can help break: The dry-soil loop · The groundwater loop · The farm-debt loop

    Active and system cooling 37

    Fans, coolers, air conditioning, cooling at scale, power during heat, and the rules that shape them. Each notes its energy, refrigerant and what happens in a power cut.

    Efficient BLDC ceiling fansActive coolingDry and humid heatMeasured in a studyAn efficient motor provides air movement with lower electrical losses than a less efficient design; the fan cools people through heat exchange rather than refrigerating the room.

    How it works

    An efficient motor provides air movement with lower electrical losses than a less efficient design; the fan cools people through heat exchange rather than refrigerating the room.

    Dry or humid heat

    Dry and humid heat. Conditional: air movement may assist body heat exchange, but benefit depends on humidity, air temperature, sweating, workload, clothing, age and exposure duration. No temperature-only guarantee of safe fan use. See fan_health_evidence.json.

    What it has done

    • reported Motor-specific occupied-room cooling or clinical effect not verified; fan-assisted building evidence is separate. India product listing, 2026-10-27. Listed product family; independent sample not reported. Limits: Do not assign fan/AC package savings to the motor alone. EESL Mart product FAQ (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Energy

    EESL supplier specification for listed BLDC products: full-speed input ≤30W; not a universal ceiling-fan value.

    Refrigerant and emissions

    Fan has no refrigerant circuit; electricity generation and embodied emissions remain relevant. Hybrid AC refrigerants would be worth assessing separately.

    In a power cut

    Stops without an energised supply unless a correctly sized solar/battery circuit is provided. Backup duration is not verified.

    The cooling-trap risk

    Poorly matched fans may leave heat exposure unresolved; when combined with AC without coordinated controls they may add load rather than reduce compressor operation. What helps: Reduce heat gains; assess user-specific limits; coordinate AC settings where appropriate and retain access to effective cooling.

    For the poorest

    Purchase/running cost shares of income not verified. Efficient watts alone do not establish affordability.

    What makes it work

    Air reaches the intended user, controls are accessible, and the heat-response plan provides another cooling route when fans are insufficient.

    What could stop it

    Unreliable supply, unaffordable purchase or electricity, obstructed airflow, unsuitable thermal conditions, inaccessible controls or unsafe installation.

    Rough cost

    • Upfront: undefined INR/unit (about US$28.36, /unit)

    Prices from 2026. Observed listing, not confirmed stock/delivery or a universal quote. No electricity tariff or upkeep price verified. EESL Mart BLDC fan listing, checked27October2026 (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Upkeep

    Owner/operator maintains safe mounting, guards/wiring and functional controls; published universal service life and cleaning interval not verified.

    Who acts

    Employers and businesses, Schools and education authorities, City and local governments, Community and civil society groups, Utilities and energy regulators. Suggested, not commitments.

    Who pays

    Possible owner, employer, public-building operator or subsidy programme; no commitment inferred.

    Fairness and risks

    Check whether women, older people, people with disabilities and tenants can control airflow and access a cooler space. Do not substitute comfort for physiological protection or use a fan to justify higher workloads. Account for noise, guards and repair access.

    Where it has been tried

    • Measured in a study Singapore office, building identity not supplied in guidebook case, May–July2016; paper2018. DC motor ceiling fans installed with altered AC operation; no isolated motor effect. One six-week office study UC Berkeley CBE author-research guidebook (opens in a new tab) ↗
    • Measured in a study BCA Zero Energy Plus office, Singapore, Renovated2019; study published2023. Ceiling and desk fans integrated with AC; distinct building within same city. One occupied office Kent/Schiavon et al., author presentation of Singapore2023 study (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Evidence

    • Reported, not evaluated EESL lists BLDC ceiling fans; input and airflow are supplier specifications, not independent thermal or health results. EESL Mart product FAQ (opens in a new tab) ↗
    • Measured in a study Singapore office research documents installed DC ceiling fans within a combined fan/AC strategy; it does not isolate BLDC motor savings. UC Berkeley CBE author-research guidebook (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Moving it elsewhere

    Hot-climate building and laboratory findings would ideally be matched to climate, age, activity, clothing and duration. High-income lab/office cases transfer testing and controls lessons, not low-income household affordability or clinical guarantees.

    Coordinated fans and higher-setpoint air conditioningActive coolingDry and humid heatMeasured in a studyFans provide local air movement while AC removes heat and moisture; coordinated operation can reduce compressor demand when users remain adequately protected and comfortable.

    How it works

    Fans provide local air movement while AC removes heat and moisture; coordinated operation can reduce compressor demand when users remain adequately protected and comfortable.

    Dry or humid heat

    Dry and humid heat. Conditional: air movement may assist body heat exchange, but benefit depends on humidity, air temperature, sweating, workload, clothing, age and exposure duration. No temperature-only guarantee of safe fan use. See fan_health_evidence.json.

    What it has done

    • measured Aggregate floor-area-normalised cooling-season compressor energy was36% lower after fan/AC staging. Hot-dry California, USA, 29-month field campaign; publication2021. 99fans,12thermostats,10buildings;13compressors in reported variability analysis. Limits: Occupied, uncontrolled setting; weather-normalised compressor changes ranged from24% increase to73% decrease. Not a universal saving or health finding. Miller et al., Energy and Buildings2021 field study (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Energy

    Study measured compressor-energy reduction; the fan input is additional and controls/occupancy affect the net result. No generic appliance W or annual household kWh inferred.

    Refrigerant and emissions

    Fans have no refrigerant; AC refrigerant and charge were not established for all examples, so system GWP is not inferred. Net emissions depend on electricity, efficiency, leakage and operation.

    In a power cut

    Stops without an energised supply unless a correctly sized solar/battery circuit is provided. Backup duration is not verified.

What helps: Reduce heat gains; assess user-specific limits; coordinate AC settings where appropriate and retain access to effective cooling.

    Powered direct evaporative air coolerActive coolingDry heatMeasured in a studyA fan draws air through wet media; evaporating water removes sensible heat from that air and adds moisture.

    How it works

    A fan draws air through wet media; evaporating water removes sensible heat from that air and adds moisture. A pump is common, though designs vary.

    Dry or humid heat

    Dry heat. Best suited to hot-dry hours; insufficient wet-bulb depression limits cooling in humid weather and the device adds humidity. Do not recommend as a sealed-room substitute for humid-climate AC.

    What it has done

    • measured Field measurements and occupant surveys informed local comfort zones; no isolated air-temperature reduction against an untreated baseline is claimed. Jaipur, India, 2019 publication; two summer seasons; exact calendar years not recovered. 1554 survey datasets across 10 offices using direct and one two-stage system. Limits: Repeated surveys may include same participants. Desk-work comfort, not occupational heat safety. Tewari et al., evaporatively cooled Jaipur offices (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Energy

    Direct cooler in the Jaipur paper was rated 350 W; not a metered operating profile or a global rating.

    Refrigerant and emissions

    Water is the evaporating working medium; no fluorocarbon refrigerant circuit in this direct-only configuration. Electricity, water and materials still have impacts.

    In a power cut

    Electrical components need a dependable supply; autonomy and backup duration are not established.

    The cooling-trap risk

    Electricity use, outdoor heat rejection and/or refrigerant loss may reinforce the cooling loop. What helps: Reduce avoidable load; choose appropriate climate/efficiency, reliable maintenance and low-impact supply.

    For the poorest

    Do not infer affordability from efficiency; obtain installed price, tariff, use hours and maintenance arrangements. Tenant and informal-worker access needs separate design.

    What makes it work

    Adequate relief airflow, reliable safe water, clean pads/tank and climate-appropriate sizing.

    What could stop it

    Humid weather, water scarcity, blocked air exits, dirty media and inaccessible maintenance.

    Rough cost

    Not publicly disclosed as a comparable installed local price in reviewed sources.

    Upkeep

    Operator cleans tank/media and maintains water/pump/fan access; schedule depends on water quality and operating season. Do not transfer a US seasonal schedule to Asia unchanged.

    Who acts

    Employers and businesses, Utilities and energy regulators, City and local governments, Community and civil society groups, Schools and education authorities, Health authorities. Suggested, not commitments.

    Who pays

    Proposed: owner/employer/public-facility budget; targeted public support or grants where people cannot afford service. No funding commitment implied.

    Fairness and risks

    Screen water competition, tank hygiene, noise and accessibility. Do not assume comfort findings establish safety for heavy work, illness or vulnerable users.

    Where it has been tried

    • Measured in a study Jaipur, India, 2019 publication. Installed direct evaporative cooling observed during field surveys. Ten office buildings overall; direct systems in all except one surveyed space Tewari et al., evaporatively cooled Jaipur offices (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Evidence

    • Measured in a study Occupied offices used direct evaporative coolers and fans with open relief paths. Tewari et al., evaporatively cooled Jaipur offices (opens in a new tab) ↗
    • Official guidance or data Official guidance distinguishes direct moisture addition and dry-climate suitability. PNNL/US DOE evaporative-cooling technical guidance (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Moving it elsewhere

    Recheck hourly climate, building load, ventilation, occupancy, water/power supply, tariffs, maintenance skills, safety and tenure. Do not transplant percentages or standards between countries.

    Known, inferred, uncertain

    Known: Installed office use and fan/pump configuration verified.

    Inferred: Taxonomy and proposed payor/operator mappings are analytical; no evaluated loop interruption claimed.

    Uncertain: Long-term thermal/health impacts, installed lifecycle cost and access for the poorest require place-specific evidence.

    Related practical actions: Homes · Outdoor and hot workplaces · Schools and childcare · Health facilities · Markets and neighbourhoods · Before summer: for municipalities

    Indirect/dew-point evaporative coolingActive coolingDry heatMeasured in a studyWater evaporates in a separate working-air stream and cools supply air through a heat exchanger, avoiding direct moisture addition to that supply stream.

    How it works

    Water evaporates in a separate working-air stream and cools supply air through a heat exchanger, avoiding direct moisture addition to that supply stream. Regenerative/dew-point designs use different airflow arrangements.

    Dry or humid heat

    Dry heat. Most useful in hot-dry conditions; humid-climate standalone capacity is constrained and it does not remove the supply-air moisture load. Two-stage indirect/direct devices do add moisture in the direct stage.

    What it has done

    • modelled Published perforated dew-point model explored geometry and airflow effects; no installed room cooling benefit or generic wattage extracted. China-based research model; climate input cases, 2025-01-06. Numerical parameter study; not occupied-building sample. Limits: Modelled optimisation is not deployment or a validated universal climate rule. Liu et al., perforated dew-point cooler model (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Energy

    Jaipur combined two-stage unit rated 550 W; this is not isolated indirect-stage consumption. Pure-IEC input power not verified.

    Refrigerant and emissions

    Evaporative-only configurations use water rather than a fluorocarbon circuit; a hybrid DX stage changes the refrigerant and electrical account.

    In a power cut

    Electrical components need a dependable supply; autonomy and backup duration are not established.

    The cooling-trap risk

    Electricity use, outdoor heat rejection and/or refrigerant loss may reinforce the cooling loop. What helps: Reduce avoidable load; choose appropriate climate/efficiency, reliable maintenance and low-impact supply.

    For the poorest

    Do not infer affordability from efficiency; obtain installed price, tariff, use hours and maintenance arrangements. Tenant and informal-worker access needs separate design.

    What makes it work

    Suitable hourly psychrometrics, maintained exchanger/pads, water supply and separate exhaust paths.

    What could stop it

    High humidity, scaling, fouling, water shortage, fan pressure losses and insufficient latent-load management.

    Rough cost

    Not publicly disclosed as a comparable installed local price in reviewed sources.

    Upkeep

    Assign a qualified operator/service provider; follow current manufacturer and local safety requirements. No universal service life or frequency established.

    Who acts

    Employers and businesses, Utilities and energy regulators, City and local governments, Community and civil society groups, Schools and education authorities, Health authorities. Suggested, not commitments.

    Who pays

    Proposed: owner/employer/public-facility budget; targeted public support or grants where people cannot afford service. No funding commitment implied.

    Fairness and risks

    Screen water quality/availability, separation of air streams and maintenance burden. Do not label two-stage indirect/direct output as humidity-free.

    Where it has been tried

    • Measured in a study Jaipur, India, 2019 publication. Installed system combined indirect exchanger with direct evaporative stage. One two-stage surveyed space within 10 office study Tewari et al., evaporatively cooled Jaipur offices (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Evidence

    • Measured in a study Published mathematical analysis; effect basis explicitly modelled. Liu et al., perforated dew-point cooler model (opens in a new tab) ↗
    • Measured in a study One surveyed Jaipur space used a two-stage indirect/direct unit; it is not a pure indirect-only field trial. Tewari et al., evaporatively cooled Jaipur offices (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Moving it elsewhere

    Recheck hourly climate, building load, ventilation, occupancy, water/power supply, tariffs, maintenance skills, safety and tenure. Do not transplant percentages or standards between countries.

    Other sources

    • PNNL/US DOE evaporative-cooling technical guidance (opens in a new tab) ↗
    • MNIT/ISHRAE EvapCal design tool (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Known, inferred, uncertain

    Known: Mechanism, numerical research and an installed two-stage composite example verified.

    Inferred: Taxonomy and proposed payor/operator mappings are analytical; no evaluated loop interruption claimed.

    Uncertain: Long-term thermal/health impacts, installed lifecycle cost and access for the poorest require place-specific evidence.

    Efficient variable-speed/inverter room air conditionerActive coolingDry and humid heatReported, not evaluatedA compressor-driven refrigerant circuit moves indoor heat outdoors.

    How it works

    A compressor-driven refrigerant circuit moves indoor heat outdoors. Variable speed matches capacity to load and can reduce cycling losses; delivered efficiency depends on the complete system and controls.

    Dry or humid heat

    Dry and humid heat. Both hot-dry and hot-humid, within rated outdoor conditions and with sufficient humidity removal; inverter is not itself proof of adequate latent cooling.

    What it has done

    • reported Illustrative label comparison reports 781.42 kWh/year for the efficient model versus 981.12 kWh/year for the comparison model. India market comparison, November 2022 report; underlying rating/price observation date not separately verified. Two commercial models: Godrej GSC18EE5GWQG and AmazonBasics AB2020INAC021. Limits: Manufacturer/label data, not household metering. Models differ in capacity, efficiency and refrigerant; cannot isolate inverter or refrigerant effect. GIZ cooling-sector mitigation guidance (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Energy

    Illustrative Indian efficient model label calculation 781.42 kWh/year; actual use depends on weather, load and operation.

    Refrigerant and emissions

    Depends on actual equipment, refrigerant and electricity supply; no whole-lifecycle zero-emission claim.

    In a power cut

    Electrical components need a dependable supply; autonomy and backup duration are not established.

    The cooling-trap risk

    Electricity use, outdoor heat rejection and/or refrigerant loss may reinforce the cooling loop. What helps: Reduce avoidable load; choose appropriate climate/efficiency, reliable maintenance and low-impact supply.

    For the poorest

    Do not infer affordability from efficiency; obtain installed price, tariff, use hours and maintenance arrangements. Tenant and informal-worker access needs separate design.

    What makes it work

    Correct load/sizing, verified seasonal rating, sound installation, maintained filters/coils and reliable power.

    What could stop it

    Upfront affordability, bills, outages, poor installation, high outdoor design temperatures and inadequate humidity control.

    Rough cost

    • Upfront: undefined INR (about US$undefined, ). Incremental price of efficient model over comparison model, not total installed price

    Prices from 2022. Historical illustrative incremental price difference in November 2022 report; underlying price observation date not separately verified. The October 2022 footnote concerns currency conversion and is not treated as the price survey date. no payback copied. GIZ cooling-sector mitigation guidance (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Upkeep

    Assign a qualified operator/service provider; follow current manufacturer and local safety requirements. No universal service life or frequency established.

    Who acts

    Employers and businesses, Utilities and energy regulators, City and local governments, Community and civil society groups, Schools and education authorities, Health authorities. Suggested, not commitments.

    Who pays

    Proposed: owner/employer/public-facility budget; targeted public support or grants where people cannot afford service. No funding commitment implied.

    Fairness and risks

    Screen landlord permission, inability to pay operating bills, noise, outdoor heat rejection and unequal access. Cooling capacity in kW is not electric demand.

    Where it has been tried

    • Simulation or test Bahadurgarh, India, October 2020 field testing;2021 report. Variable-speed-containing winning designs field tested. Prototype apartments and two baseline units RMI Global Cooling Prize testing report (opens in a new tab) ↗
    • Simulation or test Ahmedabad, India, 2020–2021 testing;2021 report. Controlled simulated-year tests; not a second occupied deployment. Laboratory prototype tests at CEPT RMI Global Cooling Prize testing report (opens in a new tab) ↗

    Evidence
